name: Arario Museum in Space
funding: Private museum founded by collector Kim Chang-il (CI Kim), funded by his Arario Corporation (bus terminal, retail, galleries).
watch: Founder-funder Kim Chang-il got a 2-year sentence for breach of duty (Daejeon court, Feb 2021); the group said it would appeal.
records_note: The museum site shows only its philosophy, exhibitions and visitor information, with no reports, accounts, funders or board.

name: Arete Foundation for Arts and Culture
funding: Small non-profit founded 2012 by Reem Gibriel, Khaled Mattawa and Nedal Swehli; AFAC grants in 2012, 2016 and 2019 (NACP National Fund).
watch: Still active in Tripoli, with a 2 Mar 2023 symposium at Dar Al Funoon.
records_note: No Arete website was located; the only records are AFAC's grantee page and an events listing, with no reports, accounts, funders or board.

name: Argos
records_note: Lists its seven-person board but posts no annual report or accounts and names only the Flemish Government as funder.

name: Arko Art Center
funding: State-run: operated by Arts Council Korea (national arts body, est.
watch: State-funded. Parent Arts Council Korea gave grant juries a political blacklist of artists in 2015, exposed in a National Assembly inspection.
records_note: No records of its own; parent Arts Council Korea posts reports 2019 to 2025, lists its council and files accounts on ALIO.

name: Armenian Center for Contemporary Experimental Art (ACCEA/NPAK)
funding: Small diaspora-funded NGO (US 501(c)(3) since 1995) with benefactors incl. Balassanian, Cafesjian, Boghossian, Hovnanian funds; state gives building free since 2002.
watch: Founded 1992 by the Balassanians. 2022 benefactor list: diaspora family funds and Boghossian (jewellery).
records_note: Its site posts no reports; it lists major benefactors as of February 2022 and its board, and its US arm files Form 990-EZ.

name: Arnolfini
funding: Arts Council England, Bristol City Council and UWE Bristol, which owns Bush House and leases the gallery space back. Ashley Clinton and Barker-Mill Trust is also credited.
records_note: Names its eleven trustees but shows funder logos only, undated, and posts no annual reports; accounts for 2020 to 2025 sit on the register.

name: Ars Aevi Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Canton of Sarajevo, City of Sarajevo, UNESCO, Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs; public cultural institution.
watch: Founded in 1992 during the Siege of Sarajevo as an act of international artistic resistance. Its permanent collection was donated by artists worldwide.
records_note: Its site has history, collection and virtual-tour pages only; no annual reports, accounts, donor list or board are published.

name: Ars Electronica Center
funding: Over 170k visitors in 2024; City of Linz and Linz AG (municipal utility) as core partners, with Siemens, KUKA, Land Oberösterreich, Dorotheum and ORF.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies, an excluded name, is a current project partner on the Center's partners page.
records_note: It posts no annual report; accounts are filed in the Austrian company register, partners show as logos, and an advisory board is named.

name: Arsenal, Volga-Vyatka branch of the Pushkin Museum
funding: Federal via the Pushkin State Museum of Fine Arts (branch since 2020); three-year cooperation agreement with Nizhny Novgorod region signed 15 Nov 2024.
watch: Founder-director Anna Gor became a Pushkin deputy director; Alexander Komarov now heads the branch.
records_note: A federal branch with no reports of its own; its Support page names sponsors and patrons. The Pushkin Museum parent site could not be read.

name: Art Gallery of Ballarat
funding: 150,607 visitors (2023-24); City of Ballarat with Creative Victoria; Ian Potter, Sidney Myer, Buckland, Helen Macpherson Smith, Gandel; McCain, Mars, NAB.
watch: Caltex (fuel retailer, now Ampol) sits on the cumulative Major Gifts roll; gift date not stated.
records_note: Ballarat has an Our donors page and no reports of its own; its parent City of Ballarat posts annual reports 2013/14 to 2024/25.

name: Art Gallery of Nova Scotia
funding: Provincial crown agency. 2024-25 supporters: Province, Arts Nova Scotia, Canada Council, BMO, Scotiabank, TD Bank Group, Ubisoft, the Sobey foundations and Benjamin Bridge winery.
watch: TD Bank pleaded guilty on 10 October 2024 to money-laundering conspiracy and Bank Secrecy Act failures, paying about $3B.
records_note: Posts annual reports from 2013-14 to 2025-26 and financial statements back to 2011-12; the 2024-25 report names supporters and the board page names directors.

name: Art Metropole
funding: Canada Council for the Arts, Ontario Arts Council, Toronto Arts Council; registered non-profit charity.
